chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who left his brother from his father and mother, and his grandfather. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth is divided between the two of them, two halves. And if there were two brothers, or a hundred, the grandfather would be with them like one of them; the grandfather receives what one of the brothers receives.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he left his sister, then for the grandfather are two shares, and for the sister is one share. And if there were two sisters, then for the grandfather is the half, and for the two sisters is the half.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he left brothers and sisters from a father and a mother, the grandfather would be like one of the brothers; for the male is the portion of two females.'
ai.seo_question: How is the grandfather's inheritance share calculated when competing with full brothers and sisters?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific inheritance share of the paternal grandfather (al-Jadd) when competing with full siblings, establishing that he is treated as a single sibling regardless of their quantity. It details distinct distributions for sisters alone versus mixed siblings, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential view that the grandfather's share is fixed relative to the number of siblings rather than being a fixed fraction like one-third. This ruling is crucial in Shia fiqh for resolving conflicts between the 'Hajb' (exclusion) and 'Shirkah' (sharing) principles regarding the grandfather's status.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who left his brother from his father and his mother, and his grandfather. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wealth is between the two of them, two halves, and had there been two brothers, or a hundred, the grandfather would be with them like one of them, whatever is attained by one of the brothers’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And if he had left his sister, so for the grandfather would be two shares, and for the sister would be a share; and if there were two sisters, so for the grandfather is the half, and for the two sisters would be the half’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And if he left brothers and sisters from a father and a mother, the grandfather would be like one of the brothers – for the males being the like of the portion of two females’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Zurarah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who leaves behind his brother from his father and mother and his grandfather.

He (the Imam) said, ‘The legacy between them is half and half. If they are two brothers or a hundred, the grandfather is with them like one of them. The grandfather with them receives a share like the share of one of the brothers.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘If he leaves behind a sister, then the shares of the grandfather are two shares and the sister receives one share, if the sisters were two, then one-half is for grandfather and one-half for the sisters.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘If he leaves behind brothers and sisters from his mother and father, the grandfather is like one of the brothers and each male receives twice as much as the share of a female.’”
